question: Should ClawSweeper own a non-blocking release-train scope reporting lane built on its existing audit, state, webhook, and Check Run machinery?
rationale: The implementation can be staged conservatively, but repository evidence cannot determine whether release-governance visibility belongs in ClawSweeper or which release contract maintainers will commit to maintaining.

options.title: Sponsor staged advisory reporting
options.body: Approve the read-only audit, durable reporting, and non-blocking release-branch check while keeping enforcement conditional on a successful future shadow train and separate admin approval.

options.title: Limit scope to local audit
options.body: Accept deterministic local Markdown/JSON classification but leave state publication, Check Runs, and dashboard visibility outside ClawSweeper.

options.title: Keep release governance elsewhere
options.body: Decline the ClawSweeper lane and retain release-scope reporting entirely in OpenClaw release tooling and maintainer process.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged advisory reporting
recommendation.body: Approve the read-only audit, durable reporting, and non-blocking release-branch check while keeping enforcement conditional on a successful future shadow train and separate admin approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice concerns release-governance ownership and policy rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
